title: How to recognise a real Hadia message
excerpt: Every real Hadia link uses hadiafrica.com. Here is how to check a message before you pay.
content_html:
Check the address

Every Hadia page and link uses hadiafrica.com. Before you pay, look at the address in your browser. If it ends in anything else, even something that looks close, such as hadia-africa.com or hadiafrica.co, it is not Hadia. Close the page and do not pay.

Check the registry code

Each registry has its own code, and the host shares it with you. To be sure a link is real, open hadiafrica.com yourself, choose Find a registry and type the code. If the same registry opens, the link was genuine.

How you pay on Hadia

  • You pay from the registry's own page on hadiafrica.com.
  • An M-Pesa prompt comes to your phone, and you enter your PIN only on that prompt.
  • If the prompt does not reach you, the page shows a paybill number and account to use instead.

What Hadia never asks for

  • Your M-Pesa PIN, in a message, on a call or on any web page.
  • Money sent to a personal phone number.
  • A code we sent you. Never read one out to anyone, even someone who says they work for Hadia.

If something looks wrong

Do not pay. Tell us through Help on hadiafrica.com, and include the link or a screenshot of the message. Tell the host too, so they can warn their guests.
